div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Step 1: In-class observation and Tier 1 supports
Teacher notes persistent struggles; implements PBIS using visuals, modeling, rules, and rewards for 4–6 weeks while gathering data.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Step 2: Support Team review and pre-referral
Teacher submits referral and data; team (TLM / Senior Teacher / TA) reviews evidence and decides next steps.
All students should be placement tested in Step 1 or Step 2 and sent to the correct level before escalating to Tier 2 (in most cases) or Tier 3
Consider all explanations for struggles including attendence, motivation, natural learning pace, etc

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Step 3: Tier 2 interventions
Teacher and TA provide small-group or one-to-one support for 4–8 weeks; progress monitored every 2–4 weeks.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Step 4: Specialist evaluation (Tier 3)
Specialist conducts a comprehensive psychoeducational evaluation covering cognitive, behavioral, and language domains.
Use culturally and linguistically appropriate tools where possible:
• Cognitive – KABC-II, Raven’s Matrices (non-verbal)
• Behavior – SDQ (Vietnamese edition available, test in L1 if possible) or *BASC-3
• Language – PPVT-4 or 5, EVT-3
Draft written report and recommendations.
Notes: Consider using EL proficiency tests such as WIDA ACCESS here and on induction to ILA for more robust tracking English learning progress;
*Tests to be interpreted cautiously if administered in English, test in L1 whenever possible

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Step 5: Eligibility and individual plan (IEP)
Team and parents review results; set goals, accommodations, services, and timeline; translate and share plan.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Step 6: Implement individualized supports (Tier 3)
Teacher and TA apply accommodations; parent partnership; staff coaching; periodic progress reviews.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Step 7: Monitor and review
Track data versus goals every 4–8 weeks; meet with parents and team; adjust plan or re-evaluate.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Refer to External Services: Clinical Psychologist, or other expert

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Legend and notes
PBIS = Positive Behavior Supports
IEP = Individual Education Plan(IEP)
Tier 1 2 3 = Universal / Targeted / Individual

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Assessment types embedded throughout
• Criterion-referenced = checks mastery of taught content (e.g., unit tests, CBM)
• Norm-referenced = compares to population norms (e.g., WISC-V, PPVT-5)
• Use cautiously if not administered in L1; translation may affect reliability, but preferred to testing in L2.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: normal; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
References
Nguyen (2019); Institute of Education Sciences (2021); PBIS Rewards (2023)
See full citations in attached submission.
